records.verificationNote: Fetched member.carefirst.com/carefirst-resources/pdf/exchange-formulary-sum7277-2026.pdf via curl and parsed locally with pypdf. Page 1 confirms 'CareFirst Exchange Formulary 2026 ... Last updated 06/01/26'. Page 103 (in-document numbering), under ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC > ANTIDIABETICS, BIGUANIDE, lists verbatim: metformin hcl tab 500mg (Tier 1, blank Requirements), metformin hcl tab 850mg (Tier 1, '$0 copay for members age 35-70 for prevention of diabetes'), metformin hcl tab 1000mg (Tier 1, blank), and metformin hcl tab er 24hr 500mg/750mg (Tier 1, blank) -- no PA, ST, or QL applies to plain metformin at any strength or release formulation. Selected metformin hcl 500mg IR as the preferred agent as the guideline-standard starting dose/formulation. The metformin-containing combination products (glipizide-metformin, pioglitazone-metformin) are also Tier 1 with no restriction; the alogliptin-metformin combination carries 'ST; PA**' (step therapy, with PA applying if step is not met) per its own line -- this restriction applies to the DPP-4 component of that combination product, not to metformin itself. Confirmed by full-document case-insensitive search that no brand name (Glucophage, Glucophage XR, Fortamet, Glumetza, Riomet) appears anywhere in the document -- fully generic-substituted class with zero brand presence and no molecule/dose absent from the formulary, so paRequired is empty. No class-wide step-therapy applies to metformin monotherapy itself; no BOGL language found near this section. [Reused 2026-10-21 for DC: same document as the MD guide (the CareFirst exchange formulary and the Kaiser Mid-Atlantic marketplace formulary cover DC, MD and VA).]

Page 1 confirms 'CareFirst Exchange Formulary 2026 ... Last updated 06/01/26'. Pages 104-105 (in-document numbering), under ENDOCRINE AND METABOLIC > ANTIDIABETICS, INSULIN, list verbatim: BASAGLAR KWP/TMP INJ 100/ML (Tier 2, blank), FIASP FLEX/INJ/PENFIL/PMPCRT (Tier 2, blank), GLARGIN YFGN INJ/SOL 100U/ML (Tier 2, blank), HUMULIN INJ 70/30, 70/30KWP, N U-100, N U-100KWP, R U-100 (Tier 3, 'OTC'), HUMULIN R INJ U-500/U-500KWP (Tier 2, blank), NOVOLIN INJ 70/30, 70/30 FP, N 100/U-100, R 100/U-100 (Tier 2, 'OTC; RELION not covered'), NOVOLOG INJ/FLEXPEN/PENFILL/MIX (Tier 2, blank), and TRESIBA FLEX INJ 100/200UNIT, INJ 100UNIT (Tier 2, blank) -- no PA, ST, or QL restriction appears on any insulin product in this list; 'GLARGIN YFGN' is the FDA nonproprietary designation for the interchangeable biosimilar glargine product (marketed as Semglee/Rezvoglar) and is selected as the preferred agent for basal glargine since it is the newest/lowest-list-price interchangeable option, though Basaglar carries identical no-PA coverage. Selected insulin glargine-yfgn as the single preferred agent representing the basal category (note: this class genuinely spans both basal and rapid-acting needs -- Novolog/Fiasp are the covered rapid-acting options, captured as alternatives, since the requested schema asks for one preferred agent per class). Confirmed by full-document case-insensitive search that Lantus, Semglee (brand name), Toujeo, Humalog, Admelog, Lyumjev, and Apidra do not appear anywhere in the 235-page text -- a substantial and clinically significant nonformulary list, since Humalog and Lantus are among the most commonly prescribed insulins nationally; CareFirst's Exchange formulary has narrowed to Basaglar/glargine-yfgn for basal and Novolog/Fiasp for rapid-acting. No class-wide step-therapy or BOGL language found near this section; the 'RELION not covered' note is a real formulary-specific restriction on Walmart's private-label human insulin, captured verbatim in the Novolin alternatives note.
